extracted_claims.text: Under Article 43, for high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III, where the provider has applied harmonised standards (Article 40) or common specifications (Article 41), the provider must choose between conformity assessment based on internal control (Annex VI) or assessment of the quality management system (Annex VII).
Annex VII sets out a conformity assessment procedure based on an assessment of the quality management system and an assessment of the technical documentation, carried out via a notified body.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to derogate from the Article 43 conformity assessment procedure and authorise placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

Article 45 requires notified bodies to inform notifying authorities of technical documentation assessment certificates and quality management system approvals issued under Annex VII, as well as any refusal, restriction, suspension or withdrawal of such certificates/approvals.

Chapter III, Section 4 of the AI Act (Articles 28-39) establishes the framework for notifying authorities and notified bodies, including notifying authorities (Art. 28), application for notification (Art. 29), notification procedure (Art. 30), requirements for notified bodies (Art. 31), presumption of conformity (Art. 32), subsidiaries/subcontracting (Art. 33), operational obligations (Art. 34), and identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (Art. 35).
The rules on notified bodies (Chapter III, Section 4) began to apply on 2 August 2025.
The remainder of the AI Act, except Article 6(1) on classification of high-risk systems, starts to apply on 2 August 2026.

The European Commission maintains the NANDO (New Approach Notified and Designated Organisations) database listing notified bodies designated by Member States under various EU regulations; it is intended to also list bodies notified under the AI Act.

A proposed Commission act, COM(2025) 836, would add a new Annex XIV with codes, categories and types of AI systems for the NANDO system and would clarify the Article 43 conformity assessment procedure where a high-risk AI system is also covered by other Union harmonisation legislation; this proposal had not been confirmed as adopted in the sources.
As of May 2026, no notified body had been formally designated under Article 29 of the AI Act in the public NANDO register for high-risk AI conformity assessment.
As of August 2026, 43 applications for AI Act notified body designation were pending across EU Member State accreditation processes.
DEKRA announced on 9 March 2026 that it had become the first accredited certification body for AI biometric systems under the EU AI Act.

Existing notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation/Directive, such as BSI, TÜV SÜD and DEKRA, are reported to be seeking designation under the AI Act for high-risk AI conformity assessment.

The European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS) has been designated as a market surveillance authority for AI systems used by EU institutions and is also designated as a notified body for conformity assessment of certain high-risk AI systems.

Manufacturers/providers of medical devices that incorporate a high-risk AI system are advised to urgently select a notified body capable of assessing both MDR compliance and AI Act technical documentation/quality management system requirements.

report:
# Conformity Assessment for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act: Procedures and Notified Body Designation Status

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a structured legal framework for conformity assessment of high-risk AI systems, offering providers a choice between internal control and third-party (notified body) assessment under defined conditions, and giving market surveillance authorities limited derogation powers (medium confidence). However, the institutional infrastructure for third-party assessment appears significantly behind schedule: as of multiple 2026 checkpoints, sources disagree on whether any notified body has been formally designated, with conflicting reports of zero designations, dozens of pending applications, and one certification body (DEKRA) claiming a "first" accreditation (low confidence, contradicted across sources).

## Key Findings

### Legal Framework for Conformity Assessment
Under Article 43, for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III, point 1, providers that have applied harmonised standards (Article 40) or common specifications (Article 41) may choose between conformity assessment based on internal control (Annex VI) or assessment via a quality management system (Annex VII) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Annex VII, where selected or required, involves a notified body assessing both the provider's quality management system and the technical documentation (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Annex 7](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). Article 46 permits a market surveillance authority to derogate from the standard Article 43 procedure and authorise market placement of specific high-risk systems for a limited period, for exceptional reasons such as public security, health, or protection of critical infrastructure (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Article 45 requires notified bodies to inform notifying authorities of certificates issued, as well as any refusal, restriction, suspension or withdrawal (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 45](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-45)).

### Institutional Framework for Notified Bodies
Chapter III, Section 4 (Articles 28–39) establishes the governance structure for notifying authorities and notified bodies, covering notification applications (Art. 29), requirements for notified bodies (Art. 31), and identification numbers/lists of notified bodies (Art. 35) (medium confidence) ([Article 28](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-28), [Article 29](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-29), [Article 31](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-31)). These rules on notified bodies reportedly began applying on 2 August 2025, ahead of the main body of the Act (excluding Article 6(1)), which applies from 2 August 2026 (low confidence) ([Future of Privacy Forum](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). The European Commission's NANDO database is designated as the registry for notified bodies across EU regulations, including the AI Act (high confidence) ([NANDO](https://ec.europa.eu/growth/tools-databases/nando); [Notified Bodies, EC](https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/single-market/goods/building-blocks/notified-bodies_en)). A proposed Commission act, COM(2025) 836, would add a new Annex XIV with AI system codes for NANDO and clarify Article 43 where high-risk AI overlaps with other Union harmonisation legislation; its adoption status is unconfirmed (medium confidence) ([Council document ST-15708-2025](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

### Current Designation Status: Contested and Unclear
Reports on actual notified body designations conflict sharply. One source states that as of May 2026, no notified body had been formally designated under Article 29 in the public NANDO register (low confidence) ([AIAuditRef](https://www.aiauditref.com/tools/notified-body-finder)). Another reports that by August 2026, 43 applications for AI Act notified body designation remained pending across Member States (low confidence) ([Think Different](https://www.thinkdifferent.blog/blog/nobody-is-ready-to-certify-europe-s-ai)). Meanwhile, DEKRA announced on 9 March 2026 that it had become the "first accredited certification body" for AI biometric systems under the Act (low confidence) ([DEKRA](https://www.dekra.us/en/dekra-becomes-the-first-accredited-certification-body-for-ai-biometric-systems-under-the-eu-ai-act)). Existing Medical Devices Regulation notified bodies (BSI, TÜV SÜD, DEKRA) are reported to be pursuing AI Act designation (low confidence) ([Agentic Library](https://agenticlibrary.net/glossary/notified-body)), and manufacturers of AI-enabled medical devices are advised to urgently secure notified bodies covering both MDR and AI Act requirements (medium confidence) ([Taylor Wessing](https://www.taylorwessing.com/en/synapse/2025/ai-in-life-sciences/selecting-your-aia-notified-body)). One source also claims the EDPS has been designated as both a market surveillance authority and a notified body for EU-institution AI systems (low confidence) ([artificial-intelligence-act.com](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
DEKRA's claimed "accreditation" (March 2026) directly conflicts with the later report of zero formal NANDO designations (May 2026) and with reports of 43 pending applications (August 2026); these discrepancies may reflect differences between accreditation, formal notification, and public registry listing, which are distinct regulatory steps. All claims regarding the current designation count are low confidence and should be treated as unresolved.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source confirms an authoritative, up-to-date NANDO list of AI Act-designated notified bodies. The adoption status of COM(2025) 836 is unknown. Whether DEKRA's accreditation equates to a formal Article 35 identification number is unclear. Conformity assessment specifics for Annex III points 2–8 and the content of Annex VI (internal control) are not detailed in available sources.
